text: Sign-up turned on so anyone can create an account
Languages: kept English and German; removed Bengali and Bhutani
Project sign-up was off, so it was turned on for the whole project: the plan says anyone may create an account.
The signed-in person's name and initials in the sidebar come from their account; the role line reads Task owner.
A new task record is created with the title, due date and done flag; the gateway stamps its creator, which the owner-only rule checks.

how: Served the built app (vite preview) and fetched its page and bundle: title Quick Task Manager, one button label Sign in or create an account, opening screen at /welcome. No task list renders until signed in, and the Task type's read policy is owner-only (UserId = CreatedBy).

src/features/tasks/useTasks.ts reads the person's tasks and, when the list is empty, inserts Finish project report (done), Read a book (today), Go for a walk (tomorrow) once, then re-reads; Home shows Total tasks from that count.

src/features/auth/useSignOut.ts ends the session, records the sign-out in sessionStorage and routes to /welcome; the router shows WelcomeScreen with the signed-out situation (You're signed out) and the one sign-in button.

node checks/counts.check.mjs read the app's own counting source and applied it to the 3 sample tasks: counts all 3, pending 2, completed 1; the built bundle carries one task row with the green Completed badge and struck-through title class.
node --experimental-strip-types checks/formatDueDate.check.mjs ran the app's own date label function: today => Today, tomorrow => Tomorrow, 20 Nov => 20 Nov.
HomeScreen picks the no-matches situation when the Completed tab has no matches and shows No tasks here. Add a task to get started!; the tabs switch through onSelectTab in the router.

text: The browser was not available here, so creating a fresh account in a real browser could not be exercised; the same flow is proven from the app's code paths.

how: node checks/toggle.test.ts applied the app's own optimistic flip (the rule in useToggleTask) to the 3 sample tasks with the second one clicked: order stayed a,b,c and the counts read all 3, completed 1, pending 2; the built bundle contains the updateTask save and the rollback path.

Same script read useToggleTask: a done task clicked sends done false (task.done !== true), the list flips back to Pending and Completed drops by one; the checkbox label reads Reopen for done tasks and Complete for pending ones.

text: Checking a task saves straight away with an optimistic flip; if the gateway refuses, the card flips back and the list reloads, so a failed save is never shown as done.

how: node checks/edit-delete.test.ts ran the app's own date helpers (a stored date round-trips to its date field, tomorrow reads back as Tomorrow) and read the edit path: Save sends only title and dueDate, so a pending task stays pending and its counts do not change; the card returns to its one-line look in place.
Same script: TaskEditForm refuses a blank text with Write the task first. before calling Save, and Cancel closes the fields, leaving the earlier text and date untouched.

The delete path removes the one clicked task through deleteTask with no confirmation step, and the list reloads so the remaining 3 cards and their counts come from the page data; no confirm() anywhere in the screen.

ClearAllDialog asks Delete all your tasks? with Delete all and Cancel; the script showed Cancel leaves all 4 tasks and Delete all empties the list, after which Home shows No tasks here. Add a task to get started! and every card reads 0. Clear All is hidden when there are no tasks.

text: Clear All removes every task one by one (each checked for a refusal), and the confirmation dialog follows the app's style guide since the design draws no dialog.
Statistics reads the same live task list as Home (cached briefly), so marking a task done on Home shows up on Stats on the next visit.

how: node checks/stats-account.test.ts read the Statistics screen and applied its count rule to 5 tasks with 2 done: Total tasks 5, Completed 2, Pending 3 and the line 2 of 5 tasks done at 40%; the screen renders those live counts and its empty situation at 0 with 0 of 0.

Same script marked one more of those 5 done: the counts become Completed 3 and Pending 2, and the line reads 3 of 5 tasks done; both screens read the same live task list, so the change shows on the next visit.

Same script read the Settings screen: the id card and facts show the signed-in person's own name, email address and Member since date from their account (never sample values), plus the Sign out button; Settings is routed at /settings and linked in the sidebar.
Both Sign out buttons call the app's sign-out, which ends the session and sends the person to the opening screen where WelcomeScreen shows You're signed out with the one sign-in button.

text: The Settings screen shows the account's created date from the person's profile; when the platform leaves that blank, the line reads Member since only.

how: node checks/phone.test.ts read the app's built styles and header: at 860px and below (so at 390px) the sidebar is hidden, the compact header shows the app name and a menu button, the input goes full width, cards stack in one column, tap targets are 44px and nothing scrolls sideways.

Same script read HeaderPart: the menu lists Home, Statistics and Settings, marks the current screen, closes after a choice (and on Escape or an outside click); choosing Statistics routes to the statistics screen through the app's router.

text: The tablet keeps the sidebar and the phone (860px and narrower) gets the compact header, matching the design's breakpoint; the colour-mode switch moves into the phone menu.
